title: Pekudei: the cloud filled it (Exodus 40:34–35)
hookLine: the presence is so full that Moses himself cannot enter

lines: THE FIRST DAY OF THE FIRST MONTH.
cards: It's the first day of the first month, in the second year since the people left Egypt. Moses sets up the sanctuary himself.

He lays the sockets, raises the boards, stretches the tent over them, puts the tablets in the ark, sets the table, lights the lamps, burns the incense, hangs the curtain at the gate, sets up the courtyard.
The text says it plainly: so Moses finished the work. Everything is in its place. And then, in the very next breath, something comes down from above that nobody built.

teach.b: In the JPS 1917 translation: "Then the cloud covered the tent of meeting, and the glory of the LORD filled the tabernacle. And Moses was not able to enter into the tent of meeting, because the cloud abode thereon, and the glory of the LORD filled the tabernacle."

teach.h: MOSES WAS NOT ABLE TO ENTER.
teach.b: Moses, who climbed into the cloud on Mount Sinai, who spoke with God face to face, as a friend, cannot walk into the tent he just built. It's too full.
The Hebrew word for glory is kavod, and at its root it means weight, heaviness. The presence here is heavy enough to fill a room so completely that there's no space left, even for Moses.
And the verb for the cloud resting on the tent, shachan, shares its root with mishkan, the dwelling, and with Shechinah, the word the rabbis later used for God's indwelling presence.
The building story has been heading here since its first command: let them make Me a sanctuary, that I may dwell among them. Now it happens.
Long after, the Book of Kings tells a similar story at the dedication of Solomon's Temple: the cloud filled the house, and the priests could not stand to minister.
Both times, the people finish every detail, and then step back, because, as the text tells it, what arrives is bigger than what they made.

how: The final verses of Exodus are read aloud in synagogue at the end of the portion Pekudei, and the idea of the Shechinah, God's indwelling presence, runs through Jewish prayer and teaching.

games.q: you're Moses. you've just set up the whole sanctuary with your own hands. the cloud comes down and the glory fills it. what happens next?
o: you walk in, as you always did on the mountain.
you can't go in: it's too full.
you call the priests to go in first.
games.why: Moses was not able to enter into the tent of meeting, because the cloud abode thereon. what he built was filled by something he couldn't make.

practice: Think of a day, a room, or a conversation you've filled to the edges, and picture clearing one small space in it: an empty half hour, a pause where you don't rush to speak. Sit inside that space for a minute without filling it.
If you pray, you can simply wait.
